title: Beetroot and Chia Pancakes
changes_from_base: Roasted beetroot purée colours a wholemeal (or teff) buttermilk batter with chia seeds folded through.
summary: Earthy beetroot pancakes speckled with chia seeds, their natural sweetness balanced with maple syrup and butter.
equipment: baking dish with lid or foil
nonstick frying pan (30 cm) or griddle

ingredients.item: large beetroot (or 2 medium), for 120 ml roasted purée
wholemeal flour or teff flour (or a mix)
buttermilk (or 240 ml yoghurt plus 120 ml milk)
butter or oil, for the pan

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C, trim the beetroot leaves to 6 mm of stalk, scrub, set in a covered dish with 1 cm water and roast until very soft, 50-60 min depending on size.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Cool the beetroot covered, trim, peel and blend until smooth, measuring out 120 ml purée.

steps.title: Sift
steps.text: Sift 125 g wholemeal or teff flour, 60 g plain flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp bicarbonate of soda, a rounded ¼ tsp salt and 1 tbsp sugar or honey if using.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Beat 2 eggs with 360 ml buttermilk, 3 tbsp oil, 1 tsp vanilla, the beetroot purée and honey if using, then quickly whisk this into the flour mix and fold in 35 g chia seeds.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Heat a griddle over medium-high heat, brush with butter or oil, drop a scant 60 ml batter per pancake and cook until bubbles break through, waiting until they hold together as they are very moist.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: Flip and cook until lightly browned, 1-2 min, moving cooked pancakes to a wire rack.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve with maple syrup and butter.

tips: Roast the beetroot covered with a little water so it steams tender without drying out.
Let the batter settle before flipping, as these pancakes are softer and moister than usual.
Measure the purée after blending so the batter has exactly 120 ml.
storage: Best eaten fresh and warm, straight from the pan. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
